findings.summary: The end-to-end tests would not compile on base if they name `UNJUDGED_PREFIX`.
findings.evidence: `UNJUDGED_PREFIX` is new in step 2. Test 2 asserts a reason starting with it, so on the base commit the test does not compile. That contradicts the claim that it 'fails on an assertion, not on compilation'. Fix: In the run_pin_tests.rs tests, assert with literal text ('unjudged', 'environment:', 'did not complete'), not new symbols.

findings.summary: The unjudged stop uses the catch-all `OtherEnvironment`, not a named StopCause.
findings.evidence: disk.rs:356-364 says a new kind of environment stop is added to StopCause once, and the known stops have named constants (LOW_DISK, CHECK_TIMEOUT, ...). The plan relies on the generic prefix branch (disk.rs:387-397). That works, but the stop has no name in the one classifier. Fix: Keep it, since disk.rs is not a deliverable. Build the reason from a pub const that starts with ENVIRONMENT_PREFIX, and propose a named VERIFIER_TIMEOUT variant in disk.rs as a follow-up in the change description.

findings.summary: The retry repeats the first run with the same inputs and deadline; reuse of the build is not shown.
findings.evidence: verification.rs:177-202: the first run already gets the same inputs, check_runs and brief, and the rerun uses the same verifier_timeout_s. I found no verifier CARGO_TARGET_DIR in verification.rs, so nothing built is shown to persist. If the verifier's own cargo work caused the timeout, the retry is likely to time out again. Fix: In the change description, state that the retry uses the same inputs and deadline, and that the unjudged, resumable outcome is the main protection. Claim build reuse only if the producer verifies it.

findings.summary: The budget refusal of the rerun is hidden behind the unjudged reason.
findings.evidence: Lines 179-184 set verifier_failure to the budget text. The plan's `.or(...)` prefers TimedOut, so that text never reaches the closing reason. Fix: When both are set, add the budget text to the unjudged reason.

summary: I read run/verification.rs, the verifier parts of verify.rs, disk.rs (StopCause, is_environment_reason, resumable_stop), run/mod.rs (failure, the check-timeout closing at 1560-1580, settle_resume_marks at 594), fake.rs, and run_pin_tests.rs (Tweak, run_with). The plan puts the fix where the fault starts. Today every non-success verifier outcome sets `verifier_failure` (verification.rs:228-234), which turns into 'did not complete' and a Rejected outcome (verification.rs:368-372; verify.rs:356, 499, 528). The plan separates TimedOut with a type, reruns once inside the existing two-run loop, and closes an unresolved timeout as Failed with an environment-prefixed reason. That reason is the path a check timeout already takes, and resumable_stop and settle_resume_marks already treat it as a resumable stop that is not a rejection. Every name the plan relies on exists. The end-to-end tests drive Athena::go with a scripted verifier turn and assert the recorded state, reason and verdict, so they would fail on base. No athena.toml field changes, and the work fits one producer run. The remaining findings are minor: use literals in the tests, do not overstate what the retry reuses, and note that the stop uses the catch-all OtherEnvironment.
